Judges the campaign/exposure-comparison requests beyond scope (data not collected), which R03's alternative accepts as reviewer_request_not_warranted; also notes the frequency text was added.
The attention check follows the treatment text and exclusion is immediate, but Table 1 gives no exclusions by condition. This is a real post-randomization attrition concern supported by the material.
Flags the duplicated Table 9 H1c label ('CR2 precaution = CR2 precaution') and its inconsistent Reject H0, left unresolved. The Table 8 p-value and equation typo are correct extras.

B.reason: Identifies the duplicate H1c row marked Reject H0 despite a non-significant CR2 effect, unresolved. The H3a argument is weak, since that interaction ran opposite to the directional hypothesis.
Judges R1 only partially resolved because the abstract sentence is unchanged. That sentence already correctly describes voluntary advice; the reference judges the issue resolved.
The wording-strength mismatch between the response ('much lower') and the text ('not fully utilized') is real but peripheral to the core claims.
Identifies the balanced relevance quota limiting the country comparison and leaves it unresolved, consistent with R08.
The Greece trust effect appears only in the adjusted model (p=.047; p=.06 unadjusted) yet is used as mechanism support. A valid overinterpretation concern.

C.reason: Effects visible only after covariate adjustment, with no multiplicity control, are interpreted substantively. Supported by Tables 6, 8 and 9.
The 'good news' trust inference rests on non-significance without equivalence testing; the self-efficacy account is untested. Substantive and supported.
Cites the relevance quota and older underrepresentation as limits on generalization, unresolved, consistent with R08.
Treats the limits-versus-voluntary distinction as visibly implemented and resolved.
Contains misreadings. The males=1 coding with negative coefficients is consistent with 'females higher'. The Table 1 page image matches the text, so there is no swap.
